gap_reasons: The delivered frontier concerns a shrinking equal-variance neighborhood, the prescribed weighted batch DIM, and count-allocation rules; it establishes neither unrestricted-estimator optimality nor allocation optimality outside that neighborhood. The evaluator proves certified computability, but the package reports no executed full-class enclosure or optimal correction at any parameter pair: the verified 779/1600 certificate covers only one ternary Gaussian subgame. Least-favorable marginals and shrinkage or reversal behavior remain algorithmically characterized rather than exhibited, and the prospective application supplies no evidence that the construction is usable at realistic roster sizes. Positioning also omits a direct comparison with [Yamin’s public two-wave minimax-regret analysis](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.16982), despite including it in the bibliography. These scope and operational limitations constrain the paper score; the open loss-uniform experiment-equivalence question is not load-bearing for V=G and does not constitute a stale headline overclaim. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]

tldr: The local excess design MSE has a limit \(V(\alpha,H)=G(\alpha,H)\), evaluated to any rational tolerance by two-sided finite certificates. A single original-pilot marginal-adaptive integer-count sequence attains it uniformly over all bounded fixed rosters. The lower certificates cover every original-record rule and retain the unknown cross-world depletion covariance.
gap: Blackwell, Pashley and Valentino establishes batch unbiasedness and conditional variance, but leaves local allocation choice at nearly equal variances unevaluated. The unresolved step is the all-record decision value when pilot evidence and remaining precision share an unobserved pairing.
fill: The output is an evaluated robust design frontier with legal prior lower certificates, uniform factual-pilot attainment and certified computation. First-order oracle efficiency, generic Gaussian minimax notation and an interval wrapper do not supply that output.
